evidence: The Tauri native supervisor is the lock authority. Manual, native-idle, restart, and corrupt-configuration lock paths advance a protected-action generation before stopping Core; protected start, retry, API, support-preview, and support-export commands check that generation before and after work so late responses are denied.

Lock events immediately replace the complete renderer document tree with a locked-only surface and clear project projection, workspace selection, command query, and open dialogs. Browser and markup tests prove project, command, diagnostics, navigation, and Core elements are absent; unlock starts a fresh Core capability and returns to no project.

Unlock uses CredUIPromptForCredentialsW with ALWAYS_SHOW_UI, DO_NOT_PERSIST, EXCLUDE_CERTIFICATES, and COMPLETE_USERNAME; LogonUserW validates the submission and EqualSid compares its token with the desktop process token. Username/domain/password buffers are volatile-cleared, handles close on every path, failures are generic and rate-limited, and cancellation remains locked.

The locked page and architecture documentation state that this is application-session protection, not Windows-account isolation. It supports the current local Windows account without a Research Observatory or cloud account and identifies same-user malware, compromised sessions/processes, capture, copied data, disk, endpoint, and physical controls as residual boundaries.

Five native application-lock tests exercise strict configuration, manual and idle lock, action invalidation, denied/cancelled/rate-limited/Core-failure reauthentication, same-user success, hidden profile identity, and bounded content-free audit. They run inside the 18-test Rust library and complete workspace clippy/test/build verification.

Frontend unit tests exercise exact native response decoding, unknown/unsupported response denial, profile-name normalization, locked project-session transitions, locked-only markup, and absence of sensitive workspace content. Browser verification additionally exercises the installed native-bridge shape and preserves all existing Projects and Diagnostics workflows.

Portable schema and security tests reject unknown fields, unsupported timeouts, weaker reauthentication/action/durable-operation/threat policies, persisted Windows identity, credential persistence flags, and missing protected-command/native-idle obligations. The broader 19-contract, 31-security, 51-desktop, 32-service, and 6-packaging suites pass.

ADR-0018 records the accepted native-supervisor boundary, alternatives, same-SID Windows reauthentication, generation/cancellation semantics, W1 stop-all durable-operation rule, recovery, residual threats, rollback, and verification duties. Its index, task link, protected paths, registry fixture, architecture document, and build inventory pass.

The strict portable profile schema/fixture fixes the allowed timeouts, conditional restart policy, native authority, same-SID authentication, protected-action policy, future explicit durable allowlist requirement, and non-isolation threat boundary. It contains no OS path or Windows account identity and is stored only under application LocalAppData.

The optional profile name, lock timeout, audit projection, reference-bound UI evidence, package schema inventory, generated planning views, security documentation, and desktop harness are updated. No project/SQLite migration is appropriate because the profile is deliberately outside projects and exports; no cloud account, remote service, new route, model/provider behavior, or future durable-worker allowlist was introduced.
